declarations.description:
A hierarchy drawn as connected cards: an organization chart, a reporting line or a team structure. Each card
shows an avatar, a label and a description, and a manager's card carries a toggle on its connector that
collapses or expands the people below it, showing how many there are while they are hidden.

The chart is drawn from data:

```ts
chart.items = [{ id: 'ana', label: 'Ana Ruiz', description: 'CEO', children: [{ id: 'li', label: 'Li Wei', description: 'CTO' }] }]
```

Every node starts expanded; `collapsed-items` lists the ones whose reports are hidden. `orientation="horizontal"`
draws reports beside their manager instead of below, which suits deep, narrow hierarchies. The chart grows to
its content and scrolls inside the host when it is wider or taller than the space it is given.

Set `selectable` to let one card at a time be selected (`value`); `item-click` fires for every card either way,
which is where an app opens a profile. `renderItem` replaces the content of every card. It is handed to Lit, so
it returns a Lit template or a DOM node, not framework markup such as JSX.

The chart is an ARIA tree with one Tab stop, and the arrow keys follow the drawing.

### Keyboard

In the vertical layout, Arrow Down expands a collapsed card, then moves to its first report; Arrow Up collapses an
expanded card, then moves to its manager. Arrow Left and Right move to the previous and next card on the same
row. The horizontal layout turns the same keys a quarter turn: Right goes in, Left goes out, Up and Down move
along the column. Home and End jump to the first and last card, and Enter or Space activates the card.

members.name: items
members.description: The root nodes, each with its reports nested in `children`. Several roots draw several charts side by side. Assign a new array to redraw: a change made inside the current one is not seen.

members.name: collapsedItems
members.description: Ids of the nodes whose reports are hidden, as a `;`-separated attribute. Every other node is expanded.

members.name: orientation
members.description: Which way the chart grows from its roots.

members.name: selectable
members.description: Lets the user select one card at a time.

members.name: renderItem
members.description: Replaces the content of every card. The card frame, its selection and focus styling and the toggle stay.

members.name: #collapsed
members.description: `collapsedItems` as a set, for the render that is in progress.

members.name: #focusWithin
members.description: Whether a card held focus when the update started, so a card that disappears hands focus on.

members.name: #entries
members.description: Where every node sits, rebuilt whenever `items` is replaced, so the methods work before the first render.

members.name: allNodes
members.description: Every node, in drawing order, collapsed or not.

members.name: getNode
members.description: The node with the given id, wherever it sits in the hierarchy.

members.name: reveal
members.description: Expands every manager above a node so its card is drawn, then scrolls the card into view.

members.name: focusItem
members.description: Moves keyboard focus to a node's card, expanding its managers first if it is hidden.

members.name: #tabStop
members.description: The focused card while it is drawn, else its nearest drawn manager, else the first card.

members.name: #drawn
members.description: The nodes of a list that are drawn: a node whose id an earlier node already took is left out.

members.name: #visible
members.description: The drawn nodes in drawing order: a collapsed node's reports are left out.

events.name: item-click
events.description: Fired when a card is clicked or activated with Enter or Space, selectable or not.

events.name: selection-change
events.description: Fired after the user selects a card in a `selectable` chart. Does not bubble: several components fire `selection-change`, so a listener belongs on the element itself.

events.name: expansion-change
events.description: Fired after the user expands or collapses a card. Does not bubble.
